q: What is meant by the "sexual division of labour"?
o: Equal wages between men and women
A system in which all work inside the home is done by women and outside work is done by men
Women reservation only in government jobs
Division of labour between agriculture and industry
e: Sexual division of labour is a system where household work is assigned to women and outside paid work is assigned to men.

q: What is the main objective of the Feminist movement?
o: Excluding men from politics
Achieving equality in personal and family life as well as public opportunities for women and men
Creating a separate country only for women
Stopping education in rural areas
e: Feminist movements aim at equality for women in personal, family, political, and professional spheres alongside men.

q: What is a "patriarchal society"?
o: Where women hold total rule
A male-dominated society that values men more and gives them power over women
Where only youth have the right to vote
A society without any family system
e: Literally rule by father, patriarchy refers to a social system that values men more and gives them power over women.

q: In which year was the Equal Remuneration Act passed in India?
e: The Equal Remuneration Act was passed in 1976 to provide that equal wages should be paid for equal work.

q: According to the 2011 Census, what was the child sex ratio (girls per thousand boys) in India?
e: According to the 2011 Census, the child sex ratio in India declined to 919 girls per thousand boys.

q: What proportion of seats is reserved for women in local self-government bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) in India?
o: One-fourth (25%)
One-third (33.3%)
Half (50% mandatory across all states)
Ten percent (10%)
e: Through the 1992 constitutional amendment, one-third of seats in local government bodies (panchayats and municipalities) are reserved for women.

q: Under the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women’s Reservation Act, 2023), what percentage of seats is reserved for women in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
o: 25 percent
33 percent
40 percent
50 percent
e: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam passed in 2023 provides 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, and Delhi Assembly.

q: "Religion can never be separated from politics" — who made this statement?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru
Mahatma Gandhi
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
Sardar Patel
e: Mahatma Gandhi said religion can never be separated from politics, meaning moral values drawn from all religions should guide politics.

q: What do "Family Laws" deal with?
o: Income tax and wealth tax
Family-related matters such as marriage, divorce, adoption, and inheritance
Only agricultural land distribution
International trade regulations
e: Laws dealing with family-related matters such as marriage, divorce, adoption, and inheritance are called family laws.

q: What type of state does the Constitution of India declare the country to be?
o: Theocratic state
Secular state
Monarchy
Military state
e: India is a secular state with no official state religion.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes "untouchability"?
o: Article 14
Article 17
Article 21
Article 32
e: Article 17 of the Indian Constitution prohibits untouchability in any form.

q: Which of the following countries has an official state religion?
o: India
Sri Lanka
United States of America
France
e: Sri Lanka (Buddhism), Pakistan (Islam), and England (Christianity) have official religions, unlike secular India.

q: When a person believes their religion is superior to others and religion should be the basis of the nation, what is this ideology called?
o: Secularism
Communalism
Feminism
Federalism
e: Communalism is based on the idea that religion is the principal basis of social community and one’s religion is superior to others.

q: Who among the following were prominent social reformers who fought against caste inequalities in India?
o: Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, Dr. Ambedkar, and Periyar
Lord Dalhousie and Curzon
Napoleon and Metternich
Adam Smith and Marx
e: Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B.R. Ambedkar, and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker advocated and worked for a society free of caste inequalities.

q: According to the 2011 Census, what was the approximate percentage of Scheduled Castes (SC) in India’s population?
e: According to the 2011 Census, Scheduled Castes accounted for 16.6% and Scheduled Tribes for 8.6% of India’s population.

q: According to the 2011 Census, what was the percentage of Scheduled Tribes (ST) in India’s population?
e: In the 2011 Census, Scheduled Tribes comprised 8.6% of India’s total population.

q: What does "Urbanisation" mean?
o: Migration from cities to villages
Shift of population from rural areas to urban areas
Expansion of only the agricultural sector
Completely shutting down industries
e: Urbanisation is the shift of population from rural areas to urban areas, which has helped weaken caste hierarchy.

q: What is "Occupational mobility"?
o: Being forced to follow the ancestral occupation across generations
Shift from one occupation to another, usually when a new generation takes up occupations other than those practiced by their ancestors
Only retiring from a job
Moving abroad from the country
e: Occupational mobility means shifting from one occupation to another, especially when a younger generation takes up jobs different from their ancestors.

q: What is meant by "Caste hierarchy"?
o: Complete economic equality of all castes
A ladder-like formation in which all caste groups are placed from the "highest" to the "lowest" castes
Ranking of government officers
List of election candidates
e: Caste hierarchy refers to a ladder-like social formation placing all caste groups from the highest to the lowest.

q: What is the full form of BAMCEF?
o: Bharatiya Agriculture and Mining Employees Front
Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation
Bengal and Maharashtra Central Education Forum
Bharat Minority Cultural Front
e: BAMCEF stands for Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation, an organisation largely of government employees campaigning against caste discrimination.

q: How does the literacy rate among women compare with men in India as highlighted in the NCERT textbook?
o: Women literacy is much higher than men
The literacy rate among women is significantly lower than among men
Both are exactly equal
Only rural men are illiterate
e: As noted in NCERT, the literacy rate among women (about 54%) has remained much lower compared to men (about 76%).

q: In which group of countries is the participation of women in public life very high?
o: Scandinavian countries (Sweden, Norway, Finland)
Middle Eastern monarchies
Central Asian nations
Only South Asian nations
e: In Scandinavian countries like Sweden, Norway, and Finland, the participation of women in public life is very high.

q: Who are the worst sufferers of communal riots in India according to human rights groups?
o: Only big industrialists
People from religious minorities
Foreign tourists
Military officers
e: Human rights groups in India have argued that most of the victims of communal riots in our country are people from religious minorities.

q: Which Fundamental Right group in the Indian Constitution gives all citizens freedom to profess, practice, and propagate any religion or not to follow any?
o: Right against Exploitation
Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28)
Right to Property
Right to Education only
e: Articles 25–28 of the Constitution provide to all individuals and communities freedom to profess, practice, and propagate any religion, or not to follow any.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth?
o: Article 15
Article 24
Article 356
Article 370
e: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

q: In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the percentage of elected women MPs reached what mark for the first time?
e: The percentage of elected women members in Lok Sabha touched 14.36% of its total strength for the first time in 2019, while in State Assemblies it is less than 5%.

q: What does a "vote bank" of a political party generally mean in politics?
o: Money deposited with the Election Commission
When a large proportion of voters from a particular caste or community vote for one party
Total number of polling booths
Storage of Electronic Voting Machines
e: A caste or community is called a vote bank when a large proportion of its voters vote for a particular party.

q: Which statement is true regarding a "Secular" state?
o: It is against all religions
It has no official religion of its own and treats all religions equally
Only majority religion citizens can contest elections
The government forces citizens to follow one religion
e: A secular state has no official religion and grants equal religious freedom to all citizens.

q: Due to reservation in Panchayats and Municipalities, roughly how many women are now elected representatives in local government bodies across India?
o: About 50 thousand
About 1 lakh
More than 10 lakh (1 million)
Only 10 thousand
e: Due to one-third reservation in local bodies, there are now more than 10 lakh elected women representatives in rural and urban local bodies across India.

q: What was a key feature of the traditional caste system in India?
o: Completely free intermarriage and job choice among all castes
Hereditary occupational division sanctioned by rituals
Annual legal change of occupation
A class system based purely on income
e: In India, the caste system was a hereditary occupational division sanctioned by rituals, where members of the same caste formed a social community.

q: Generally, what kind of social structure exists in Indian society regarding gender roles?
o: Matriarchal
Patriarchal (male-dominated)
Completely egalitarian
None of these
e: Ours is still a male-dominated, patriarchal society where women face disadvantage, discrimination, and oppression in various ways.

q: What does a Time Use Survey reveal about women’s daily work in India?
o: Women work fewer hours than men
On an average, an Indian woman works one hour more than an average man every day, yet much of her work is unpaid
Women only do outside salaried jobs
Men and women spend equal hours in unpaid housework
e: On average, an Indian woman works one hour more than a man daily, yet most of her domestic work is unpaid and often not valued.

q: Despite the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976, what is observed about women’s wages across almost all areas of work?
o: The law applies only to central ministries
In almost all areas from sports and cinema to factories and fields, women are paid less than men for the exact same work
Women refuse to accept full wages
The Act was repealed in 1980
e: Even though the Equal Remuneration Act exists, in almost all areas of work—from sports and cinema to factories and fields—women are paid less than men.

q: What is the primary cause of the child sex ratio falling below 850 or even 800 in some Indian states?
o: Preference for sons by parents leading to sex-selective abortion of girls before birth
Migration of young girls abroad
Biological impossibility of female births
Higher education among women
e: In many parts of India, parents prefer to have sons and find ways to have the girl child aborted before she is born, causing a sharp decline in the child sex ratio.

q: What is the share of women in State Legislative Assemblies in India?
o: About 33%
About 25%
Less than 5%
About 50%
e: In State Assemblies across India, the share of women representatives has remained less than 5%.

q: Which statement is correct regarding the practice of Census in India?
o: Every ten years the Census records the religion and SC/ST status of each Indian citizen
Census in India is conducted every year
Women are excluded from the Census
Census covers only urban areas
e: The Census of India records the religion and Scheduled Caste/Tribe status of every Indian once every ten years.

q: According to the 2011 Census of India, which religious community constituted about 79.8% of the population?
o: Muslims
Hindus
Christians
Sikhs
e: According to the 2011 Census, Hindus accounted for 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, Christians 2.3%, and Sikhs 1.7% of the population.

q: According to the 2011 Census, Muslims constituted roughly what percentage of India’s population?
e: In the 2011 Census, Muslims made up 14.2% of India’s total population.

q: Gandhiji believed that politics must be guided by ethics drawn from religion. What did he mean by "religion" here?
o: Rituals of only one specific sect
Moral values that inform all religions
Political rule by priests
Exclusion of other religions
e: By religion, Gandhiji did not mean any particular religion like Hinduism or Islam, but moral values that inform all religions.

q: What has the Women’s movement demanded regarding "Family Laws" in India?
o: Complete abolition of all family relations
Reform of all religious family laws to remove discrimination against women and make them more equitable
Granting divorce rights only to men
Banning courts from hearing family disputes
e: Women’s movements argue that family laws of all religions discriminate against women and have demanded that government change these laws to make them more equitable.

q: What is the most common everyday expression of communalism?
o: Armed riots
Everyday beliefs involving religious prejudices, stereotypes of religious communities, and belief in the superiority of one’s religion
Cancellation of elections by the Election Commission
Providing reservation to minorities
e: The most common expression of communalism is in everyday beliefs involving religious prejudices, stereotypes, and belief in superiority of one’s religion over others.

q: In India, communalism in the majority community often takes what form?
o: Desire for a separate political unit
Majoritarian dominance
Dissolving Parliament permanently
Boycotting all elections
e: For those belonging to the majority community, communalism takes the form of majoritarian dominance, whereas for a minority community it can take the form of a desire to form a separate political unit.

q: Which is the ugliest and most extreme form of communalism?
o: Communal violence, riots, and massacre
Use of sacred symbols
Organising religious gatherings
Comparative study of different religions
e: Sometimes communalism takes its most ugly form of communal violence, riots, and massacre, as seen during the 1947 Partition.

q: Despite being a secular state, why does the Indian Constitution allow the state to intervene in the matters of religion?
o: To declare one religion as the official state religion
To ensure equality within religious communities, for example by banning untouchability
To close down all temples and mosques
To impose religious taxes
e: The Indian Constitution allows the state to intervene in matters of religion in order to ensure equality within religious communities, such as banning untouchability.

q: What was the main objective behind the constitutional prohibition of untouchability?
o: Ending caste discrimination and ensuring equality within religious communities
Levying new taxes only in rural areas
Changing the calendar
Attracting foreign companies
e: Untouchability was prohibited to eliminate caste-based discrimination and ensure social equality for all citizens.

q: According to the 2004–05 NSSO sample survey cited in NCERT, Other Backward Classes (OBCs) constituted roughly what share of India’s population?
o: About 16%
About 25%
About 41%
About 65%
e: The 2004–05 National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) estimated the population of Other Backward Classes (OBCs) to be around 41%.

q: Which factor has contributed to breaking down the old notions of caste hierarchy in modern India?
o: Large-scale urbanisation, growth of literacy and education, and occupational mobility
Banning inter-caste marriages
Strengthening the landlord system
Restricting entry into cities
e: Economic development, large-scale urbanisation, growth of literacy and education, occupational mobility, and the weakening position of landlords have broken down old caste hierarchy.

q: Why does caste hierarchy matter less in day-to-day urban interactions compared to rural areas?
o: Because in urban areas people travel together in buses/trains and eat together in restaurants without knowing each other’s caste
Because there are no laws in cities
Because only one caste lives in cities
Because marriages do not happen in cities
e: In urban spaces like buses, trains, offices, and restaurants, people interact, work, and eat side by side regardless of caste.

q: Why has caste NOT completely disappeared from contemporary India?
o: Most people still marry within their own caste or tribe, and centuries of advantages and disadvantages continue to shape education and economic status
Because the Constitution promotes caste discrimination
Because urbanisation has completely stopped
Because there were no social reformers
e: Endogamous marriage within one’s own caste persists, and historic caste advantages or disadvantages continue to reflect in education and wealth.

q: How did the principle of "universal adult franchise" and "one-person-one-vote" impact caste in Indian politics?
o: It compelled political leaders to mobilise and seek support from castes hitherto treated as inferior and brought new consciousness among them
It deprived Dalits of voting rights
It gave extra votes to landlords
It abolished elections
e: One-person-one-vote forced political leaders to gear up to mobilise castes once treated as low, awakening political consciousness among them.

q: What has been a positive outcome of the expression of caste differences in politics?
o: It has given many disadvantaged communities (Dalits and OBCs) space to demand their share of power and gain better access to decision-making
It established one-party dictatorship
It shut down all schools
It reduced voter turnout to zero
e: Expression of caste differences in politics has helped disadvantaged groups like Dalits and OBCs gain better access to decision-making, dignity, and resources.

q: What can be a negative consequence of exclusive attention to caste in politics?
o: It can divert attention from pressing issues like poverty, development, and corruption, and sometimes lead to tensions, conflict, and violence
It immediately doubles the national GDP growth rate
It instantly makes all castes equal
It permanently eliminates corruption
e: Exclusive attention to caste can divert attention from vital issues like poverty, development, and corruption, and can also lead to tensions and violence.

q: What is a common example of "Caste in politics"?
o: Political parties keeping in mind the caste composition of a constituency when choosing candidates for elections
Companies selling shares in the stock market
Selecting fast bowlers for a cricket team
Printing the Union Budget in Parliament
e: Considering the caste composition of constituencies while nominating candidates and ensuring caste representation in governments are forms of caste in politics.

q: How does "Politics in caste" operate?
o: Each caste group tries to become bigger by incorporating neighbouring castes or sub-castes and enters into coalitions with other caste groups
The Election Commission dissolves castes
Every caste votes for a single person nationwide
Castes remain completely isolated from politics
e: Politics influences the caste system as caste groups absorb neighbouring sub-castes, form coalitions with other castes, and create new categories like "backward" and "forward".

q: What is the broad historical relationship between caste status and economic status in India?
o: There is no relationship between the two
The disproportionately large presence of "upper castes" among the urban middle classes and poorer sections containing larger shares of historically disadvantaged castes
All disadvantaged castes are extremely wealthy
Only upper castes fall below the poverty line
e: Although both rich and poor exist in every caste today, historical advantages ensure upper castes remain disproportionately represented in the urban middle class and wealthier groups.

q: Why is it incorrect to say that elections in India are all about caste and nothing else?
o: Because no parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of one single caste, nor does any party win votes of all voters of a caste
Because voting by caste is banned by police
Because candidates are all from one family
Because India has a one-party system
e: No parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of one caste, voters also weigh government performance and leader popularity, and ruling MPs/MLAs often lose.

q: According to the definition of feminism, can a man also be a feminist?
o: No, only women can be feminists
Yes, any woman or man who believes in equal rights and opportunities for women and men is a feminist
Only government officers can be feminists
Only unmarried persons are feminists
e: A feminist is a woman or a man who believes in equal rights and opportunities for women and men.

q: Which key areas did Feminist movements focus on beyond political rights?
o: Only on sports tournaments
Enhancing women’s political and legal status, improving educational and career opportunities, and demanding equality in personal and family life
Only on tax cuts
Stopping military recruitment
e: Radical women’s movements aimed at equality in personal and family life as well, alongside improving educational, career, and political status.

q: Under what condition does the expression of religion in politics become dangerous and divisive?
o: When religion is seen as the basis of the nation and state power is used to establish the domination of one religious group over the rest
When the government reforms family laws to make them fair
When moral values drawn from all religions guide politics
When citizens peacefully celebrate festivals
e: Religion becomes dangerous in politics when it is seen as the basis of the nation and state power is used to establish one religious group’s domination over others.

q: What key demographic observation does NCERT highlight about religious population shares in India since Independence (1961–2011)?
o: Muslims, Christians, and Sikhs grew to become the majority
The overall balance of different religious communities has not changed dramatically over the decades; total shares shifted only marginally
The Hindu share dropped to 30%
All religious minorities disappeared
e: NCERT notes that since 1961, the proportion of different religious communities has remained broadly stable (Muslim share increased only slightly by ~3–4%), refuting fears of drastic demographic shifts.

q: What has been the most visible result of the sexual division of labour on public life?
o: Women’s role in public life, especially politics, has remained minimal in most societies
Women gained monopoly over all industries
Men became confined solely to household chores
Every country elects only women prime ministers
e: Although women constitute half of humanity, their role in public life, especially politics, has been minimal in most societies due to the sexual division of labour.

q: Men readily work as tailors or cooks in hotels outside, yet rarely stitch clothes or cook at home. What does this illustrate?
o: Men lack biological ability to cook
Gender division is not based on biology but on social expectations and whether work is paid
Working in hotels is compulsory by law
Women cannot operate sewing machines
e: When domestic tasks like cooking or tailoring become paid jobs outside, men willingly take them up—showing the sexual division of labour is social, not biological.

q: How does India’s representation of women in the national parliament compare with many developing countries in Africa and Latin America?
o: India ranks first globally
India lags well behind several developing nations in Africa and Latin America
African and Latin American countries have zero women MPs
India and Sweden have identical percentages
e: India has been among the bottom group of nations in the world regarding women’s representation in national parliaments, lagging behind the global average and several African/Latin American nations.

q: Which factor explains why the proportion of women among highly paid and valued jobs is still very small in India?
o: High drop-out rates among girls as many parents prefer to spend resources on their boys’ education
Government ban on women entering higher education
Companies hiring only retired persons
All women leaving agriculture
e: Despite performing equally well or better in school, many girls drop out because parents prefer to spend limited resources on their sons’ education.

q: Before the passing of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam in 2023, what was the long-standing demand of women’s organisations?
o: Legally reserving at least one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
Abolishing Panchayati Raj institutions
Giving voting rights exclusively to women
Extending Lok Sabha tenure to 10 years
e: Women’s organisations had long demanded a fair proportion of seats—at least one-third—to be legally reserved for women in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

q: Identify the legitimate and healthy instance of religion entering politics as discussed in NCERT:
o: Demanding protection of religious minorities from violence and reforming discriminatory religious family laws
Spreading hatred through religious slogans to win votes
Stripping voting rights of one religious group
Enforcing one religion’s symbols upon all schools
e: Bringing moral values, minority protection, and fair reform of family laws into politics is healthy as long as the state treats every religion equally and prevents oppression.

q: What is the fundamental flawed assumption underlying communal thinking?
o: That followers of one religion share identical secular interests and people of different religions cannot live together as equal citizens in one nation
That every person speaks a different language
That democracy requires regular elections
That all religions preach peace
e: Communalism wrongly assumes that followers of one religion have identical interests and cannot share equal citizenship with others; in reality, people of the same religion have many varied voices and interests.

q: How does communalism operate through "political mobilisation" on religious lines?
o: Using sacred symbols, religious leaders, emotional appeals, and plain fear to unite voters of one religion in the political arena
Debating purely economic policies
Signing international trade treaties
Making election expenses transparent
e: Political mobilisation on religious lines involves the use of sacred symbols, religious leaders, emotional appeals, and plain fear to bring followers of one religion together politically.

q: Which combination accurately reflects the constitutional foundations of Secularism in India?
o: (i) No official religion, (ii) Freedom of religion, (iii) Prohibition of religious discrimination, (iv) State intervention to ensure equality within religions
(i) Official majority religion, (ii) Voting only for minorities, (iii) Allowing untouchability, (iv) Press censorship
(i) Mandatory atheism, (ii) Total ban on religious traditions
(i) Religious leaders holding reserved seats in Parliament
e: Indian secularism rests on: no official religion, freedom to profess/practice/propagate (or none), prohibition of discrimination on religion, and state intervention for intra-religious equality.

q: Why is a secular Constitution alone NOT sufficient to combat communalism?
o: Because communal prejudices and propaganda in everyday life and religion-based mobilisation in politics must be actively countered
Because the Constitution does not apply to elections
Because India lacks an independent judiciary
Because the Constitution expires every five years
e: Communal prejudices and propaganda need to be countered in everyday life and religion-based mobilisation needs to be countered in the arena of politics alongside a secular constitution.

q: How is the caste system in India distinct from the occupational division found in all societies?
o: Unlike normal division of labour, India’s caste system made occupational division hereditary, sanctioned it by rituals, and enforced endogamy and social exclusion
Other societies lack any occupations
Indian caste system was based purely on university degrees
Other societies banned marriage altogether
e: Caste was an extreme form of hereditary occupational division sanctioned by rituals, enforcing endogamy (marriage within caste), dining restrictions, and exclusion/untouchability.

q: What is the contemporary consequence of historical inequalities in access to education across castes in India?
o: Castes that had access to education under the old system naturally progressed in modern education and the urban middle class, while barred castes lagged behind
Upper castes are confined exclusively to landless labour
All historically excluded castes achieved 100% literacy
Education has zero link to economic status
e: Castes that had access to traditional education moved ahead in acquiring modern education and dominate the urban middle class, while barred castes fell behind.

q: Which example demonstrates the LIMITS of caste in deciding Indian elections?
o: Rich and poor voters or men and women from the same caste often vote differently, and sitting MPs/MLAs frequently lose despite caste calculations
In every election the candidate from the largest caste always wins
All voters blindly vote for their caste leader
Political parties never release manifestos
e: Sitting MPs and MLAs frequently losing elections—and rich and poor within the same caste voting differently—proves elections are not decided solely by caste.

q: Politics is not only influenced by caste, it also reshapes the caste system. Which example illustrates this?
o: Emergence of new kinds of caste groups like "backward" and "forward" and coalitions formed across caste groups in the political arena
All castes migrating to a single village
Government prescribing wedding rituals
Indefinite postponement of elections
e: In politics, caste groups enter into coalitions and new broader categories such as "backward" and "forward" emerge in the political arena.

q: In a constituency, multiple parties may field candidates from the same dominant caste. What is the consequence for voters of that caste?
o: Voters of that caste end up with more than one candidate from their caste, while many other castes have no candidate from their caste at all
All votes of that caste are automatically cancelled
The Election Commission halts polling
Only one party can contest
e: Many political parties put up candidates from the same caste if it dominates an area, leaving voters with multiple choices from that caste or none from their own.

q: If voters’ attachment to political parties is stronger than their attachment to their caste, how do they usually vote?
o: They prioritise their preferred political party’s policies and performance over a candidate’s caste
They boycott polling
They only vote for independent candidates
They only press NOTA
e: Voters often have strong attachment to political parties which is stronger than their attachment to their caste or community.

q: Why is communalism considered a major threat to democracy, whereas expression of caste identity in politics has sometimes helped disadvantaged groups?
o: Communalism seeks domination or separation based on religion threatening national unity, whereas caste mobilisation has often helped excluded Dalit and OBC groups claim dignity and power
Communalism deals strictly with inflation
Caste politics never causes disputes
The Constitution encourages communalism
e: While exclusive identity politics harms democracy, caste expression helped excluded groups demand rights, whereas communalism inherently challenges equal citizenship and secular unity.

q: How does democratic politics turn caste competition into broader social coalitions?
o: Since no single caste can win an election on its own, parties and caste groups are forced to negotiate and build alliances with other castes and communities
Because all castes are legally merged into one name
Because only 10 people contest elections
Because Parliament bans coalition politics
e: No party can win using a single caste, forcing parties and caste groups to win the confidence of multiple castes and communities through dialogue and alliances.

q: Which combination highlights the main spheres where gender inequality manifests in India?
o: Literacy rate, unpaid housework, unequal wages for equal work, child sex ratio, and legislative representation
Only railway fares and postage rates
Only weather forecasting and sports rules
Only space exploration
e: Women’s disadvantage in India appears prominently in literacy gaps, unpaid work burden, wage disparity, declining child sex ratio, and low legislative representation.

q: Comparing the political expression of gender, religion, and caste divisions in India, which statement is most accurate?
o: Political expression of gender division has helped improve women’s status, whereas religious expression must be guarded against communalism to preserve equality
Political expression of gender has had only negative effects
Communalism benefits women the most
Caste has zero interaction with politics
e: Political mobilisation on gender has largely aided women’s empowerment and representation, whereas religious mobilisation easily slips into divisive communalism unless kept secular.

q: How can it be said that it is NOT politics that gets caste-ridden, rather it is caste that gets politicised in India?
o: For political power, caste groups widen their base, negotiate alliances with other castes, and create new categories like "forward" and "backward" in the political arena
Because castes run the Election Commission
Because all politicians belong to one single caste
Because castes remain strictly confined to scriptures
e: Politics also transforms caste as caste groups reshape themselves by merging sub-castes, forming coalitions, and creating broader political categories like "forward" and "backward".

q: Which statement accurately reflects why the makers of the Indian Constitution chose the model of a secular state?
o: Because communalism was recognised as a major challenge to democracy, requiring equal freedom for all faiths with no official religion
Because India had no religious diversity
As a condition for foreign commercial loans
To ban citizens from visiting temples or mosques
e: Recognising communalism as one of the biggest challenges to democracy in a diverse country, the makers of our Constitution chose the model of a secular state.

q: Why is increasing women’s political representation considered crucial in a democracy?
o: Because unless women control power as elected representatives, issues related to women’s well-being will not get adequate attention
So that men are banned from contesting elections
So that Panchayats can be abolished
So that all taxes are abolished
e: Feminists argue that unless women control power, their problems will not get adequate attention; hence having more women as elected representatives is vital.

q: If a district’s child sex ratio drops sharply from 930 to 840 between 2001 and 2011, which social factor is primarily responsible?
o: Son-preference mentality and sex-selective female foeticide
Opening of new factories in cities
Higher enrolment of girls in secondary schools
Increase in agricultural output
e: Preference for sons leading to sex-selective abortion of girl children is the primary reason why the child sex ratio has fallen below 850 in several regions.

q: Which statement correctly reflects the issue of safety and harassment of women highlighted in NCERT?
o: Urban areas have become particularly unsafe for women, and they are often not safe even within their own home from beating and domestic violence
Domestic violence exists only in developed nations
Urban areas are completely free of safety issues for women
All crimes vanished automatically after passing laws

e: Jotiba Phule fought against caste inequalities and championed education for marginalised castes and women.

q: What common communal myth is directly refuted by India’s decadal Census statistics on religious populations from 1961 to 2011?
o: The myth that minority populations will overtake the majority and drastically alter the overall demographic balance of religious communities
The fact that multiple religions exist in India
The fact that a census occurs every ten years
The fact that India has a large population
e: Census data from 1961 to 2011 show that the overall population balance of religious communities has remained broadly stable, refuting fears of drastic demographic takeover.

q: How does the unpaid nature of household work affect women’s social status under the sexual division of labour?
o: Because women’s household labour is unpaid, society overlooks its value and treats it as less important than men’s outside paid work
Women receive double wages for household chores
Domestic chores are already counted as 90% of GDP
Men pay legal salaries to homemakers
e: Even when women work outside for income, their household work remains unpaid and largely unrecognised, undervaluing their total labour.

q: Which statement accurately describes BAMCEF as discussed in NCERT?
o: An organisation largely made up of government employees that campaigns against caste discrimination
A trade union exclusively for private bank managers
A regional political party contesting elections
A religious trust building temples
e: BAMCEF (Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation) is an organisation largely of government employees that campaigns against caste discrimination.

q: If an election survey shows 55% of a caste voted for Party A and 45% for Party B, while women voted differently from men due to a welfare scheme, what does this prove?
o: Caste "vote banks" are not monolithic; people of the same caste have different interests by class, gender, and assessment of government schemes
Caste has disappeared completely in that district
Party A engaged in rigging
Elections are decided solely by gender
e: Even when a caste is called a vote bank, all its voters never vote identically; gender, economic class, and welfare performance split votes within any caste.

q: "In Indian politics, religion is neither completely banned from public ethics nor granted official state status." Which principle captures this balance?
o: Indian Secularism, ensuring equal respect and non-discrimination alongside reformist intervention for equality
Complete Theocracy
Strict State Atheism
Majoritarianism
e: Indian secularism balances equal freedom and respect for all religions with non-discrimination and reformist intervention against intra-religious inequality.

q: Which set contains ONLY positive constitutional/legal measures strengthening gender equality in India?
o: Equal Remuneration Act (1976), one-third reservation in local bodies (1992), Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (2023), Article 15 ban on sex discrimination
Equal Remuneration Act (1976), legalising sex-selective tests, local body reservation
Keeping discriminatory family laws unchanged, Article 15
Restricting girls’ college entry, 1992 reforms
e: Equal Remuneration Act (1976), 1992 local reservation, 2023 Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, and Article 15 all promote gender equality.

q: According to NCERT, what is the overall impact of urbanisation on caste in India?
o: Urbanisation has significantly weakened everyday caste hierarchy and untouchability in public life, even though caste still persists in areas like marriage
Urbanisation increased untouchability tenfold
Inter-caste marriage is legally compulsory in cities
Urbanisation has zero impact on caste
e: Urbanisation weakened rigid day-to-day caste hierarchy in public spaces, though endogamy in marriage and historical disparities still persist.

q: Which action would be COUNTERPRODUCTIVE for a democratic society fighting communalism?
o: Making the majority community’s religious symbols mandatory across all government schools
Publicly countering communal prejudices and propaganda
Legally penalising parties that seek votes through religious fear and hatred
Promoting inter-community dialogue and secular civic education
e: Enforcing majority religious symbols in state schools promotes majoritarianism and undermines secular equality, worsening communal division.

q:
Match the 2011 Census demographic categories with their exact population shares:
A. Hindus
B. Muslims
C. Scheduled Castes (SC)
D. Scheduled Tribes (ST)
e: In the 2011 Census, population shares were: Hindus 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, SCs 16.6%, and STs 8.6%.

q: Which pair best captures BOTH the positive and negative sides of caste expression in democratic politics?
o: Positive: Giving disadvantaged castes access to decision-making and dignity; Negative: Diverting attention from poverty/corruption and causing tension or violence
Positive: One-party rule; Negative: Universal adult franchise
Positive: Encouraging untouchability; Negative: Increasing urbanisation
Positive: Stopping occupational mobility; Negative: Raising literacy
e: On the positive side, caste politics gave disadvantaged groups voice and representation; on the negative side, exclusive caste focus diverts attention from development and fuels conflict.

q: Why did the makers of the Indian Constitution adopt a secular state with joint electorates instead of religious communal electorates?
o: Because separate religious electorates deepened communal division and went against equal democratic citizenship across faiths
Because only one religion existed in India
Because elections are held every five years
Because joint electorates do not require polling
e: Having witnessed communal division before 1947, India chose secular equal citizenship with joint constituencies rather than divisive religious separation.

q: Which assessment of the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 is most accurate based on real-world Indian conditions discussed in NCERT?
o: While the law mandates equal wages for equal work, in practice women are still paid less than men across fields from sports and cinema to factories and farms
Since 1976 there has been zero wage gap anywhere in India
The Act applied exclusively to foreign companies
The law requires women to accept lower pay
e: Despite the legal mandate of the 1976 Act, women continue to be paid less than men across almost all areas of work.

q:
What key trends characterise caste in contemporary Indian politics?
1. Negotiations and alliances between different castes have become essential to win elections.
2. Economic disparities and government performance split voters within the same caste across parties.
3. Upper castes alone unilaterally decide every election outcome.
Choose the correct option:
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
All 1, 2 and 3
e: Statements 1 and 2 are true; statement 3 is false as universal adult franchise compels broad cross-caste alliances.

q: A student concludes: "Since the Indian Constitution banned caste discrimination, caste no longer affects the life chances of any Indian citizen." How would you evaluate this conclusion?
o: It is flawed because despite constitutional prohibition, centuries of historical advantage and disadvantage still reflect in educational, economic, and social disparities today
It is 100% correct because historic inequality vanished instantly in 1950
It would only be wrong if India lacked a Constitution
It is correct because endogamy has completely vanished
e: While constitutional bans ended legal sanction, historic disparities in education, wealth, and ongoing endogamy mean caste still shapes social and economic outcomes.

q: What is the overarching democratic lesson of the chapter "Gender, Religion and Caste"?
o: Expression of social diversity is natural in democracy: political mobilisation for gender and caste justice can strengthen democracy, whereas constant secular vigilance is essential against divisive communalism
Democracy should be run exclusively by one religion and one caste
Economic growth requires keeping women out of politics
The Constitution must outlaw all forms of diversity
e: Democracy accommodates social diversity—political mobilisation can empower women and disadvantaged castes toward equality, while secularism guards against communal division.
